ICD-O prints skin beside it and names vulva, penis, scrotum and prostate as other primary sites (Rule H, Table 23).

conflicts.issue: ICD-O-3.2 prints C44 beside Malignant chondroid syringoma (8940/3), yet ICCC-2017 places 8940/3 and Myoepithelial carcinoma 8982/3 in XIIa4 at every site. Both are referred to Group XII.
A skin case with no tissue, or cytology with malignant cells and no type, records 8000/3 or 8001/3, which ICCC-2017 places in XIIb at these sites. The tree refers it to Group XII.

Kaposi sarcoma (IXc) and dermatofibrosarcoma (IXd5) arise in skin; the Group IX tree codes them and decides the behaviour of 8832 (8832/1 is Dermatofibrosarcoma protuberans, NOS; 8832/3 is the fibrosarcomatous form).
Cutaneous lymphomas (IIb3) and Langerhans cell histiocytosis (IId) are coded from the Group II tree at the skin site (Rule D).
Leukaemia in the skin records C42.1 (Rule E); myeloid sarcoma (Ib) keeps the skin site.
Melanoma is XId at every site; the skin histology screen and the clinical and cytology screens hand over to the melanoma tree.

ICCC-2017 makes C51.9 vulva NOS, C60.9 penis NOS and C63.2 scrotum XIe, while C51.0-C51.8 and C60.0-C60.8 are XIf10. If the vulva and penis carcinoma part serves these sites, the subgroup computed from the site gives XIe at C51.9, C60.9 and C63.2 whichever tree is used; the skin tree offers the three sites only so a case is never stranded. 8085 and 8086 (HPV positive and negative squamous cell carcinoma) sit in no ICCC range at these sites and come from that part's sources, not this one.
Paget disease, mammary sits in the ICCC XIe range at skin but is a breast code by its printed site; it belongs to the breast tree.

data_gaps.need: Paediatric occurrence (ages 0 to 18) of Merkel cell carcinoma, the adnexal carcinomas (pilomatrical, porocarcinoma, sebaceous, microcystic adnexal, digital papillary) and the named subtypes of basal cell and squamous cell carcinoma
data_gaps.why: Huang 2019 and Kaloga 2016 make basal cell carcinoma (8090/3) and squamous cell carcinoma (8070/3) options. Neither names Merkel cell carcinoma, an adnexal carcinoma or a basal cell or squamous cell subtype, so those codes stay in the picker. Pfister 2022 lists Gorlin syndrome and xeroderma pigmentosum as paediatric predisposition syndromes (PDF p. 19).
